stem:
Ojas opens a dried pea seed and finds two cotyledons. The seedling later has netted leaf veins and a thick central root. He also opens a rice grain and finds one cotyledon. In class he learns that two cotyledons mark a dicotyledon (reticulate venation, taproot) and one cotyledon marks a monocotyledon (parallel venation, fibrous roots).

Answer both parts.

parts.text: How should he classify the pea plant?

options.text: dicotyledon with reticulate venation and a taproot
dicotyledon with parallel venation and a taproot
monocotyledon with parallel venation and a fibrous root system
monocotyledon with reticulate venation and a taproot

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Two cotyledons mark a dicotyledon, which has reticulate venation and a taproot.

teacher.key_rationale: Two cotyledons identify a dicotyledon with reticulate venation and a taproot. Parallel venation with a taproot mixes terms; monocot labels reverse the pea’s seed type.
